newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil barges dip, one pct cargoes strong.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil barges dip, one pct cargoes strong.

text.p: European high sulphur fuel oil barges fell on Tuesday with aggressive selling of storage material by an independent, while one percent cargoes fetched a strong number, traders said.

After early trades at $93.50 fob ARA an independent trading house sold at $93 some 10,000 tonnes of stored material, before going at 25-cent increments to $93.75 later in the day. Monday's only trade was done at $94.50.
"There was very aggressive selling by the trading house, up to 25,000 tonnes today," one trader said.
Traders said that at the end of the day a major came in with a stronger bid at $94.50 for refinery material but no sellers were found at that price.
"No one is going to sell refinery material at that level, it is more expensive," a trader said.
Low sulphur cargoes fetched a good number with a European refiner selling a cargo to a refiner at fob high NWE plus $1.75. The 25,000-tonne cargo is for prompt loading, traders said.
Few other sellers were heard offering, with most said to be opting to fetch higher prices in the near future with a contango between swaps and prompt physical cargoes.
